sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes parts of the neck and back, a section of the hip bone, and thirteen connected tail bones along with scattered ribs.
This single-species genus, Punatitan coughlini, comes from the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
Researchers suggest a possible connection between Punatitan and the contemporary Bravasaurus regarding the titanosaur egg concentration found at the site.
Phylogenetic analysis places Punatitan as a derived member of the Lithostrotia within the clade Aeolosaurini, a subclade of Rinconsauria.
Although it was recovered within a group containing two Aeolosaurus species, researchers did not assign it to that genus due to doubts regarding the placement of Aeolosaurus maximus.
It lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
